title: Replace the obsolete in-memory messaging kernel
description:
The in-memory control-plane kernel (python/src/chatticus/control_plane.py) implements the rejected design in its messaging and realtime paths. It must be replaced or bypassed for the durable computerless turn, not extended.

What is obsolete:

- post_message always enqueues frozenset({"computer"}) for an addressed bot. Challenge 5 says many turns never need a computer; a computerless worker must be able to take a turn. The capability set must come from the turn, not be hardcoded.
- RealtimeSubscription and TurnStream are an in-process fan-out held by the control plane. Challenge 1 deleted persistent sockets and in-process rendezvous; the rendezvous is a DynamoDB chunk store polled by a streaming function, and the stream is scoped to one turn.
- There is no turn_id, no turn attempt, no lease, and no fencing. The ownership work in epic chatticus-65398905 needs those primitives.

What is not obsolete and should be preserved:

- Worker registration, tenant ownership, heartbeat, cost-class routing, computer affinity and pinning, approvals and auto-review rules, and the snapshot publish/relocate/hydrate paths. These encode the worker protocol that survives.

Acceptance criteria:

- The durable computerless turn path (task chatticus-df6e93c2) does not reuse RealtimeSubscription or TurnStream.
- A turn job's required capabilities are not hardcoded to computer; a computerless worker can take a turn.
- The obsolete thread and in-process stream specifications are removed, not kept as a second supported path (task chatticus-a8f9d17c).
- The routing/approval/snapshot kernel paths that survive keep their tests.

Related: chatticus-a8f9d17c (replace the obsolete specs), chatticus-df6e93c2 (implement the durable computerless turn path), chatticus-65398905 (recover turns without duplicate actors).
